*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the
social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20
(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

 Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting
  of January 19, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  C l e r k / S e c r e t a r y a t aphillips@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org . To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and
  in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence
  should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to
  the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
  Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public
  can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5
  minutes prior.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from
  landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it
  is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission.
  Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.
  l Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed below for the
  respective City Council Dates:
  ¡ January 12, 2021 - Access Code: 2743141#
  ¡ January 19, 2021 - Access Code: 2025334#
  ¡ January 26, 2021 – Access Code: 2453970#

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting;
however, members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access
options 1 and 2 noted above.

Inglewood, California
  January 19, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  January 19, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:03 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority
  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agenda.
  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Agenda Item Nos. 3, 4, and DR-1.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  January 15, 2021, in the amount of $4,785,692.14 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1) Alejandro Alers for alleged property, inadequate gopher control on June 1, 2020.
  2) Ike Gent for alleged personal injury/property damage, motor vehicle collision on June
  19, 2020.
  3) Maria Granados for alleged personal injury; trip and fall on April 24, 2020.
  4) Victor Lara for alleged vehicle towed on October 29, 2020.
  5) Adrian Torres for alleged property damage; fire hydrant on June 20, 2020.

  B. Reject Insufficient Claim Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1) Eleanor Hayles for alleged property damage; Metro Rail construction on unknown
  date.

  C. Return Late Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 911.2.

  1
   1) Shirley Brown for alleged pre-sale report on December 15, 2017.
  2) Emily Castaneda for alleged tree roots in 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby: 1) Reject Claims listed as A1 through A5; 2) Reject
  Insufficient Claim listed as B1; and 3) Return Late Claims listed as C1 and C2. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 21-49 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-
  2021 BUDGET APPROVING FUNDS FOR THE SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE
  INVESTMENT BOARD, INC. Staff report dated January 19, 2021, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Budget
  approving funds in the amount of $44,500 for the South Bay Workforce Investment
  Board, Inc. to continue operating, enhancing the Inglewood Teen Center, by providing
  virtual services during the pandemic.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-49 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2020-2021 BUDGET TO PROVIDE FUNDING FOR THE
  INGLEWOOD TEEN CENTER

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 21-50 ADOPTED – AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO SIGN
  SERCO, INC. REQUEST TO ASSIGN AGREEMENT NO. 14-142 TO LAZ KARP.
  Staff report dated January 19, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a
  resolution authorizing the Mayor to sign SERCO, Inc.’s request for consent to assign
  Agreement No. 14-142 to LAZ Karp Associates, LLC.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-50 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO SIGN SERCO, INC.’S
  REQUEST FOR CONSENT TO ASSIGN AGREEMENT NO, 14-142 TO LAZ
  KARP ASSOCIATES, LLC

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  BID NO. RFB-0127 REJECTED – POLICE SERVICE EQUIPMENT AND
  SUPPLIES.  Staff report dated January 19, 2021, was presented recommending
  rejection of all bids received for Police Service Equipment and Supplies, per Bid No.
  RFB-0127.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject all bids; and 2) Direct staff to re-advertise
  the aforementioned bid document and proceed with a competitive re-bid process. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
 142  RESOLUTION NO. 21-51 ADOPTED – BORROWING OF FUNDS FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2020-2021 AND THE ISSUANCE AND SALE OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD 2021 TAX AND REVENUE ANTICIPATION NOTE. Staff report
  dated January 19, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution providing
  for the borrowing of funds for Fiscal Year 2020-2021 and the issuance and sale of the
  City of Inglewood 2021 tax and revenue anticipation note in an aggregate amount not to
  exceed $10,000,000.

  Peggy Velasquez, Revenue Supervisor, gave an oral report.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 21-50 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION PROVIDING FOR THE BORROWING OF FUNDS FOR
  THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 AND THE ISSUANCE AND SALE OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD 2021 TAX AND REVENUE ANTICIPATED NOTE
  IN AN AGGREGATE AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $10,000,000, AND
  APPROVING THE EXECUTION OF A NOTE PURCHASE AGREEMENT
  RELATING TO SUCH NOTE AND AUTHORIZING OTHER ACTIONS IN
  CONNECTION THEREWITH

  and 2) Approve and authorize the form, execution, and delivery of a note purchase
  agreement between the City of Inglewood and Bank of America, N.A.; and 3) Authorize
  other subsequent actions in connection therewith. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  ORDINANCE NO. 21-04 ADOPTED – AMENDMENT TO INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 11.  Staff report recommending adoption of
  Ordinance No. 21-04 approving the following amendments to Inglewood Municipal Code
  Chapter 11, A) Deleting Article 17 (Residential Solar Permitting) in its entirely, and
  replacing it with an updated Article 17; and B) Adding Article 18 (Electric Vehicle
  Charging Stations Expedited Review Process) to adopt an expedited, streamlined
  permitting process for electric vehicle charging stations as required by Assembly Bill
  1236.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the further reading be waived. The motion was carried out by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that Ordinance No. 21-04 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA 1)
  DELETING ARTICLE 17 (RESIDENTAL ROOFTOP SOLAR SYSTEM
  EXPEDITED PERMITTING) OF CHAPTER 11 IN ITS ENTIRETY AND
  REPLACING IT WITH AN UPDATED ARTICLE 17; 2) ADDING ARTICLE
  18  (ELECTRIC  VEHICLE  CHARGING  STATION  EXPEDITED
  PERMITTING) TO CHAPTER 11 (BUILDING REGULATIONS) TO ADOPT
  AN EXPEDITED, STREAMLINED PERMITTING PROCESS FOR ELECTRIC
  VEHICLE CHARGING STATIONS AS REQUIRED BY LAW.

  which was introduced at the meeting held on January 12, 2021, be adopted. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
 PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

Cheryl Arnold, cousin of Andrew Summerfield, spoke concerning the reward from the
City Council.

Eddie Cruz, Inglewood resident, spoke in support of the “Here to Stay Campaign” for
Inez Torres.

Rick Ford, Lennox/Inglewood Tenant Union, spoke regarding tenant and homeowners
rights to prevent evictions during the pandemic.

Yvonne Figueroa, organizer with LA Voters, spoke supporting Inez Torres, and requested
a meeting with the City Council.

Tristian Lucas, Inglewood resident, spoke concerning homeowners rights and requested
support from the City Council.

Janice Ayala, daughter of Inez Torres, called to request support from the City Council to
help her family get their house back.

Rio (No last name given), spoke in support of the “Here to Stay Campaign.”

Milan Moore, called regarding the reward for Andrew Summerfield.

REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha Thompson, reported that she
received emails regarding the reward for Andrew Summerfield and the Here to Stay
Campaign for Inez Torres.

There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
adjourned in memory of Kevin Childress, Hermina “Minnie” Galvan, and Juan Aria at
the hour of 3:02 p.m.

Approved this 29th day of June, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

________________________
James Butts, Jr., Mayor
